deep.reconstruction:
CONTEXT. The page is undated, but the next folio carries receipts and a letter draft from Pisa (winter semester 1863/64), so it is probably from that time. The previous folio sets up products of theta functions such as a_1 = ϑ234bc·ϑ234au·ϑ234av·ϑ234aw. It also introduces the complement rule ab12 = 34cuvw.

The characteristic labels are subsets of the ten symbols {1,2,3,4,a,b,c,u,v,w}, taken modulo complement.
- Even-size subsets label half-periods (ab12 ~ 34cuvw).
- 5-subsets label the theta functions ϑ234bc, ϑu1234, ...
- 3-subsets appear in the products 12u·abu.

This matches the classical labeling of the 2^8 characteristics of a hyperelliptic curve of genus 4 by subsets of its 10 branch points (C(10,5)/2 = 126 non-vanishing even thetas, 10 vanishing even ones, 120 odd ones). It may equally be Riemann's own symbolic bookkeeping; the page does not say which, so this identification is my inference.

(1) DEFINITIONS (top). The table
  abc | u v w
  a: bc au av aw
  b: ac bu bv bw
  c: ab cu cv cw
  uvw: abcuvw vw uw uv
is a 4x4 scheme of labels. Prefixing the index set complementary to ν (234 for ν=1, etc.) to the row entries gives four products of four thetas:
- α_1 = ϑ234bc ϑ234au ϑ234av ϑ234aw (row a);
- δ_1 (written like 'v_1') = ϑ(·) ϑ234vw ϑ234uw ϑ234uv (row uvw; the first factor is 234abcuvw, i.e. the singleton {1});
- by implication β_ν, γ_ν come from rows b and c.
He then sets p = ∏_ν α_ν β_ν γ_ν δ_ν and K^4 = p^{1/4}·sqrt(ϑ(u)/ϑ(u1234)). There is also an expression α_1^2 = sqrt(...) of a product of seven quantities; it is not fully legible.

(2) SIX-TERM LINEAR RELATIONS. The first is
(α_1/α_2)·1u + (α_1'/α_2')·1v + (α_1''/α_2'')·1w + (α_2/α_1)·2u + (α_2'/α_1')·2v + (α_2''/α_1'')·2w = 0.
Primes mean u is replaced by v, w. The other five are listed for the index pairs (2,3), (3,1), (3,4), (1,4), (2,4). Each is tagged by the complementary pair (3/4, 1/4, 2/4, 1/2, 2/3, 3/1). These are presumably theta relations (Riemann/Thomae type) whose terms 'iu' are theta expressions; their derivation is not on the page. Later an analogous relation tagged c/uvw appears: Σ (α_1/β_1)·au + ... + (β_1/α_1)·bu + ... .

(3) ABSTRACT LINEAR-ALGEBRA STRUCTURE (the core of the page). Unknowns a_i, b_i, c_i, d_i (i = 1..4) carry weights α_i, β_i, γ_i, δ_i. They satisfy:
- (i) Σ_L (λ_i/λ_j) L_i L_j = 0 for i ≠ j, e.g. (α_1/α_2)a_1a_2 + (β_1/β_2)b_1b_2 + (γ_1/γ_2)c_1c_2 + (δ_1/δ_2)d_1d_2 = 0;
- (ii) a_i^2 + b_i^2 + c_i^2 + d_i^2 = s^2;
- (iii) a_1^2 + ... + a_4^2 = s^2.

In my notation, put A = [L_i/λ_i] and B = [L_i λ_i] (rows i, columns L = a,b,c,d). Then (i)+(ii) say exactly B·A^T = s^2·I. Hence A^{-1} = B^T/s^2 and A^T B = s^2 I as well, so (iii) is automatic.

Riemann states det A = s^4/K^4; this is the input that brings in K. Consequences:
- det B = s^8/det A = s^4 K^4.
- Inverse/cofactor relation for A: the (4,a) cofactor of A equals det A·(a_4α_4)/s^2. This gives his α_4 a_4 s^2 = K^4·|b_i/β_i, c_i/γ_i, d_i/δ_i|_{i=1..3}.
- The same relation for B gives (a_4/α_4)·s^2 = K^{-4}·|b_iβ_i, c_iγ_i, d_iδ_i|.
- The cofactor sign (-1)^{4+1} is suppressed.

(4) LINEAR SUBSTITUTION. The rows of A define y ↦ x by Σ_L (L_i/λ_i)·y_L = (s/K)·x_i. Its inverse is K s·y_1 = Σ_ν a_ν α_ν x_ν, and similarly for y_2, ... . He wrote 'c_ν γ_ν x_ν' for y_2 where b_ν β_ν is meant, or else it is a generic row. Square roots he wrote first are struck out. The normalisation s/K makes the substitution unimodular: det((K/s)A) = (K/s)^4·s^4/K^4 = 1.

(5) JACOBI COMPLEMENTARY MINORS. He writes
((a_1b_2)/(α_1β_2) − (b_1a_2)/(β_1α_2))·K^4 = c_3d_4γ_3δ_4 − c_4d_3γ_4δ_3.
This is Jacobi's theorem: a 2x2 minor of A equals det A times the complementary minor of A^{-1} = B^T/s^2, i.e. (s^4/K^4)(1/s^4)·(minor of B). The sign is +.

(6) LAST LINES. The complementary pairing ab12 = cuvw34 is used to pair 3-sets: 12u with abu ↔ 34u with cvw; 1a·2b, 2a·1b, 3c·4uvw, 4c·3uvw. He then begins sums of products of odd thetas weighted by the 2x2 data:
- (α_1β_2/K^2)·12u·abu + ... + K^2·34u·cvw/(α_1β_2) + ...
- (K^2/(γ_3δ_4))·12u·abu + ... + (γ_3δ_4/K^2)·34u·cvw + ...
These are evidently meant to be equated or compared via the Jacobi identity of (5). They are unfinished.

PURPOSE (my reading). Riemann is showing that the coefficients of his six-term theta relations, built from products of theta values, form a 'weighted orthogonal' 4x4 system. Equivalently, there is a unimodular linear substitution whose matrix and inverse are given by the same theta products, with K^4 as the determinant normaliser.
errors: Cofactor signs are suppressed: the minor for entry (4,a) carries the factor (-1)^{4+1}. The formulas α_4a_4s^2 = K^4·det(...) and a_4s^2/α_4 = K^{-4}·det(...) hold up to sign, i.e. with a suitable column order.
In the inverse substitution 'K s y_2 = c_ν γ_ν x_ν' should read b_ν β_ν x_ν (or it is meant generically).
Square roots in the substitution formulas are struck out. The final normalisation x_i·s/K, K s y = B^T x is consistent and unimodular.
Condition (iii) (column sums of squares) is not independent: it follows from (i)+(ii). This is harmless.
det A = s^4/K^4 is asserted, not derived on this page; it presumably comes from the theta definitions of K and p. The six-term theta relations are likewise stated without proof.

results.what: The weights α_i, β_i, γ_i, δ_i (products of four theta values) and entries a_i, ..., d_i satisfy B·A^T = s^2 I, with A = [L_i/λ_i] and B = [L_iλ_i]. The coefficient matrix of the theta relations is thus orthogonal up to a diagonal weighting, with det A = s^4/K^4.
results.modern_name: Orthogonal (weighted-orthogonal) matrices whose entries are theta functions/theta constants
results.usually_credited_to: H. Weber (1878, Crelle 84, Kummer surface: genus-2 thetas give orthogonal 4x4 substitutions); F. Caspary (1880s); also Frobenius

results.what: Cofactor/inverse formulas for A and B in terms of each other.
results.modern_name: Adjugate (cofactor) formula for the inverse matrix

results.what: Normalising so the substitution x ↦ y is unimodular: det((K/s)A) = 1, with inverse K s y = B^T x.
A 2x2 minor of A times K^4 equals the complementary 2x2 minor of B.
Six-term linear relations among theta products for each index pair, with coefficients α_i/α_j etc.; complement labeling of characteristics by subsets of 10 symbols (ab12 = cuvw34).
results.modern_name: Hyperelliptic theta relations / Rosenhain–Thomae subset notation for characteristics (Riemann theta formula type identities)
results.usually_credited_to: Rosenhain (genus 2), Thomae (1870), Riemann's theta formula (published via Prym 1882)

deep.surprise_reason: The linear algebra itself is routine: weighted orthogonality, cofactors, Jacobi's minor theorem. The interesting point is the context. It suggests Riemann (c. 1863/64, Pisa) was organising theta-function relations, apparently in a 10-symbol (genus-4 hyperelliptic-type) labeling, into orthogonal 4x4 substitutions with theta-product entries. That connection is usually associated with Weber (1878) and Caspary in the genus-2 case. The theta side is only sketched and not derived here, so the evidence is suggestive rather than a clear priority claim.

checkable.asserts: Setup: B = s^2 (A^T)^{-1} encodes the weighted-orthogonality conditions B A^T = s^2 I.
Row conditions imply column conditions (A^T B = s^2 I), so Σ_i a_i^2 = s^2 is automatic.
det A · det B = s^8; hence det A = s^4/K^4 gives det B = s^4 K^4.
Cofactor of entry a_4/α_4 equals det A · (a_4 α_4)/s^2, i.e. α_4 a_4 s^2 = K^4 · cofactor (Riemann's formula up to sign).
Dual formula: a_4 s^2/α_4 = K^{-4} · cofactor of B.
Jacobi complementary minors: with det A = s^4/K^4 this is (a_1b_2/(α_1β_2) - b_1a_2/(β_1α_2))K^4 = c_3d_4γ_3δ_4 - c_4d_3γ_4δ_3.
The substitution normalised by s/K is unimodular when det A = s^4/K^4.
Inverse substitution: K s y = B^T x solves A y = (s/K) x.

transcription_corrections: 'v_1 = ϑ( ) ϑ234vw ϑ234uw ϑ234uv' is the fourth weight (row uvw), presumably δ_1. Its first factor corresponds to 234abcuvw = complement {1}.
In 'K s y_2 = c_ν γ_ν x_ν' the intended expression is Σ_ν b_ν β_ν x_ν (or generic).
The fractions 3/4, 1/4, 2/4, 1/2, 2/3, 3/1 at the left margin are labels: the index pair complementary to the pair used in each relation. They are not numerical coefficients.
The square roots after 'x_1' and 'K s y_1' are struck out by Riemann; the surviving forms are x_ν·s/K and K s y_1 = Σ a_ν α_ν x_ν.
The lowercase letters a_1, b_1, ... in the orthogonality relations are distinct from the Greek weights α_1, β_1, ...; the machine transcription mostly preserves this.
